The font is set in code: the module-level `_STYLE` CSS declares `@font-face { font-family: Inter; src: url(assets/Inter.woff2) }` and `body { font-family: Inter }`, using a shared `FontConfiguration`. Change the font there. Note: HTML(string=...) is called without base_url, so the relative `assets/Inter.woff2` URL may not resolve, and WeasyPrint then silently falls back to a system font.
toolu_01JF82f9r6fPSnEaorzmEPhr.summary: Invoice PDFs: WeasyPrint in src/billing/pdf.py; font set via @font-face in _STYLE (not the Dockerfile)

content.text:
Invoice PDFs are rendered by **WeasyPrint**, and the font is set in code, in `src/billing/pdf.py`.

**What renders them:** `render_pdf()` at `src/billing/pdf.py:14` renders the HTML with WeasyPrint. It only runs when the `invoice-pdf-v2` flag is on, and `flags.toml:3` has it on. The old wkhtmltopdf renderer has been removed; calling it now just raises an error.

**Where to change the font:** in `_STYLE` at `src/billing/pdf.py:8-11`:
```python
_STYLE = CSS(
    string="@font-face { font-family: Inter; src: url(assets/Inter.woff2); } body { font-family: Inter; }",
    font_config=_FONTS,
)
```
To switch fonts, edit the `@font-face` rule and `body { font-family: ... }` there.

**Likely cause of the wrong font:** the PDFs probably aren't getting Inter at all.
- **The font file isn't in the repo.** There's no `assets/` directory and no `.woff2`, `.ttf` or `.otf` file anywhere in the repo.
- **The path is relative with no base to resolve it.** `HTML(string=html)` is called without a `base_url`, so WeasyPrint has nothing to resolve `assets/Inter.woff2` against. Even if the file existed, it probably wouldn't load.

When WeasyPrint can't load a `@font-face` source it doesn't error. It falls back to whatever system font is available, which matches the problem you're seeing.

**To fix it:** add `Inter.woff2` to the repo, then point to it with an absolute path. Either use a `file://` URL built from `Path(__file__).parent / ...`, or pass `base_url=` to both `CSS(...)` and `HTML(...)`. Running WeasyPrint with logging on will show a "failed to load font" warning, which confirms the cause.

**Project memory:** the stored note on this was out of date. It said rendering used wkhtmltopdf and that fonts had to be fixed in the Dockerfile. I've updated it to describe the WeasyPrint setup.

content.text:
One real gap, plus one thing that was my own mistake rather than a tool limit.

1. **`update` has no `evidence` or `source_file` parameter, and doesn't change provenance.** When I rewrote the invoice PDF memory (`01a0fcc2-45f2-…`), I wanted to record why it changed: `src/billing/pdf.py` uses WeasyPrint, not wkhtmltopdf, and `flags.toml` has `invoice-pdf-v2 = true`. I also wanted to show that an agent made the change. `update` only takes the new content, and the memory still says `source: shared/human`, so a reader would think a human wrote my corrected text. I'd want `evidence` and `source_file` on `update`, like `challenge` has, or a `source`/`edited_by` field that changes automatically when an agent edits a human-authored memory. I'd have used it to keep a record of who changed the memory and based on what.

2. **Not a tool gap, my mistake:** I could have kept the old version's history by calling `challenge` (with `source_file: src/billing/pdf.py`) and then `create` with `supersedes`. Instead I overwrote it in place with `update`. The tools allowed this; I just took the shortcut. A combined option would make the right path easier, for example `update` with `supersede: true`, which would close the old version and create the new one in a single call.
